From 9d72732fe70c11424bc90ed466c7ccfa58b42a9a Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Johan Hovold <johan@kernel.org>
Date: Tue, 14 Apr 2026 15:43:19 +0200
Subject: [PATCH] spi: topcliff-pch: fix use-after-free on unbind

Give the driver a chance to flush its queue before releasing the DMA
buffers on driver unbind

Fixes: c37f3c2749b5 ("spi/topcliff_pch: DMA support")
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org	# 3.1
Cc: Tomoya MORINAGA <tomoya-linux@dsn.okisemi.com>
Signed-off-by: Johan Hovold <johan@kernel.org>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260414134319.978196-9-johan@kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Mark Brown <broonie@kernel.org>

diff --git a/drivers/spi/spi-topcliff-pch.c b/drivers/spi/spi-topcliff-pch.c
index c120436434d0..14d11450e86d 100644
--- a/drivers/spi/spi-topcliff-pch.c
+++ b/drivers/spi/spi-topcliff-pch.c
@@ -1410,9 +1410,6 @@ static void pch_spi_pd_remove(struct platform_device *plat_dev)
 
 	spi_unregister_controller(data->host);
 
-	if (use_dma)
-		pch_free_dma_buf(board_dat, data);
-
 	/* check for any pending messages; no action is taken if the queue
 	 * is still full; but at least we tried.  Unload anyway */
 	count = 500;
@@ -1436,6 +1433,9 @@ static void pch_spi_pd_remove(struct platform_device *plat_dev)
 		free_irq(board_dat->pdev->irq, data);
 	}
 
+	if (use_dma)
+		pch_free_dma_buf(board_dat, data);
+
 	pci_iounmap(board_dat->pdev, data->io_remap_addr);
 
 	spi_controller_put(data->host);
-- 
2.34.1

## Summary of the Patch

### Modifications in Each File

**File:** `drivers/spi/spi-topcliff-pch.c`

- **Removed** the call to `pch_free_dma_buf(board_dat, data)` from its original location (just after `spi_unregister_controller()` and before the wait loop for pending messages).
- **Added** the same `pch_free_dma_buf()` call **after** the wait loop that drains the message queue and after freeing the IRQ (but still before unmapping and releasing the controller).

### Relationship Between the Modifications

The change reorders the cleanup steps in the driver’s remove function. The original code freed DMA buffers while there might still be pending DMA transfers in the queue, leading to a **use-after-free** bug. By moving the DMA buffer deallocation **after** the loop that waits for pending messages to complete, the patch ensures that:

1. All pending transfers are allowed to finish (or the driver at least attempts to drain the queue).
2. The DMA buffers remain valid for any final cleanup or completion callbacks.
3. Only then are the DMA buffers safely freed.

This prevents accessing freed memory in DMA-related code paths during driver unbind, fixing the use-after-free vulnerability.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
<text>
if (use_dma)
    pch_free_dma_buf(board_dat, data);
</text>
Reason:
The DMA buffer free was called before waiting for pending messages (the while loop that checks the queue). This allowed transfers still in progress to access freed memory, causing a use-after-free.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
<text>
if (use_dma)
    pch_free_dma_buf(board_dat, data);
</text>
Reason:
The free is now placed after the wait loop for pending messages and after freeing resources and disabling interrupts (pch_spi_free_resources, free_irq). This ensures no ongoing transfers are using the buffers when they are freed, eliminating the use-after-free.
